brief:
A British court will decide whether five activists face terrorism sentencing for vandalising a Barclays bank branch, Al Jazeera English reported. The case marks an unusual application of terrorism law to protest-related vandalism, according to the outlet's framing.

The defendants are accused of damaging the bank in what prosecutors characterize as a terrorism-related offense. If convicted under terrorism statutes rather than standard criminal charges, they could face significantly harsher penalties. The legal classification of the vandalism has drawn attention from observers monitoring how protest activity is prosecuted in UK courts.
dek: Court to rule on whether five activists accused of vandalising a Barclays bank will face terrorism sentencing.
title: UK court weighs terrorism charges against Palestine activists
